full_name_ar: سلمة بن أبي سلمة بن عبدالأسد ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba describes him as the stepson (rabib) of the Prophet; Ibn Ishaq's Maghazi has Umm Salama carrying him in her lap on the hijra. Via 'Abdullah ibn Shaddad, Ibn Ishaq reports that Salama gave his mother Umm Salama in marriage to the Prophet, who married him to Umama bint Hamza while both were young children. Al-Waqidi, followed by Abu Hatim, claimed he lived until the caliphate of 'Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan, while Ibn al-Kalbi said he is reported to have died before consummating with Umama.

full: Zaynab bint Uthman bin Maz'un b. Habib b. Wahb b. Hudhafa b. Jumah b. 'Amr b. Husays b. Ka'b
full_name_ar: زينب بنت عثمان بن مظعون الجمحية ( رضي الله عنها
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba gives her as Zaynab bint 'Uthman ibn Maz'un al-Jumahiyya. In the Prophet's time both Ibn 'Umar and al-Mughira ibn Shu'ba sought to marry her; her uncle Qudama favoured Ibn 'Umar (his nephew through Zaynab bint Maz'un) while her mother favoured al-Mughira. Citing Ibn Sa'd via Nafi', it relates that after her father's death Qudama married her to Ibn 'Umar, but she and her mother told the Prophet she did not consent, he annulled the marriage, and she then married al-Mughira ibn Shu'ba. No death year is given.

The quoted author says earlier compilers did not list him, but he includes him because his father died in Medina in year 2 and his mother was also in Medina, so he was certainly alive in the Prophet's lifetime and several years old. No death year is given.

full: Khalid ibn Ribah habshi
full_name_ar: خالد بن رباح الحبشي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 2166) gives him as Khalid ibn Rabah al-Habashi, brother of Bilal the muezzin, with the kunya Abu Ruwayha. Ibn Sa'd reports that a brother of Bilal sought to marry an Arab woman and her family agreed on condition Bilal attend. Ibn Manda records Bilal asking 'Umar to let him settle in Syria with 'my brother Abu Ruwayha, whom the Prophet made my brother', and that they settled at Darayya among Khawlan; Ibn Hajar comments this suggests Abu Ruwayha was Bilal's brother in Islam rather than by lineage. No death year is given.

full: Durrah/Fakhita bint Abi Lahab ibn 'Abd al-Muṭṭalib b. Hashim b. 'Abd Manaf b. Qusayy b. Kilab

bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 11154) gives her as Durra bint Abi Lahab ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib al-Hashimiyya, the Prophet's paternal cousin, who accepted Islam and emigrated. Ibn 'Abd al-Barr says she married al-Harith ibn Nawfal ibn al-Harith ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, while Ibn Sa'd says she married al-Harith ibn 'Amir ibn Nawfal (killed at Badr as a non-Muslim) and afterwards Dihya ibn Khalifa al-Kalbi. A weak report (via 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Bishr) relates that on arriving in Medina as an emigrant she stayed in the house of Rafi' ibn al-Mu'alla, and when women taunted her about her father the Prophet addressed the people from the pulpit defending his kin. No death year is given.

full_name_ar: زيد الخيل بن مهلهل الطائي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: A pre-Islamic hero of Tayy with the kunya Abu Mikanf, known as a poet, orator and generous man. He came to the Prophet and embraced Islam in 9 AH; the Prophet praised him and renamed him Zayd al-Khayr and granted him land in Najd. After seven days in Medina he fell ill with fever and died on the way back to Najd at a watering place called Farda. The page draws on al-A'lam, Usd al-Ghaba, al-Isaba, al-Wafi bi al-Wafayat, al-Isti'ab and al-Thiqat.

full_name_ar: الحصين بن الحارث بن المطلب ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Al-Husayn, of Quraysh (Banu al-Muttalib), was the brother of 'Ubayda (martyred at Badr) and al-Tufayl. He fought at Badr and in all the campaigns with the Prophet. The page gives several death dates: 33, 31, 32 or 30 AH, including one report that he died in 32 AH a few months after his brother al-Tufayl. It draws on al-Isti'ab, Usd al-Ghaba, al-Isaba, Ibn al-Athir's al-Kamil, al-Tabaqat al-Kubra and A'yan al-Shi'a.
research_evidence: الحصين بن الحارث بن المطلب ابن عبد مناف بن قصي القرشي المطلبي توفي سنة 33

full: Mu'awiyah ibn al-Harith b. al-Muttalib b. 'Abdul Muttalib
full_name_ar: معاوية بن الحارث بن المطلب بن عبد المطلب ( رضي الله عنه
bio: The page, quoting Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba, says Ibn Ishaq mentioned him in his Sira as a devoted defender of the Prophet. Abu Talib is reported to have mourned him in verse. His brothers were 'Ubayda, al-Tufayl and al-Husayn, and he apparently left no descendants. Note: the page gives his lineage as al-Muttalib ibn 'Abd Manaf, while our record reads 'ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib'.

Since 'Ubayda was martyred at Badr, Ibn Hajar infers that this son was a Companion, and suggests he probably died in the Prophet's lifetime. Ibn al-Athir (Usd al-Ghaba) says he died near puberty in the Prophet's lifetime, while Ibn 'Asakir records an opinion that he was killed at Yarmuk; the page gives 8 AH as his death year.

Citing Usd al-Ghaba, it relates via Ibn 'Abbas that the Prophet saw her as a child and said he would marry her if she grew up in his lifetime, but he died first. full_name_ar: المغيرة بن نوفل بن الحارث ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn al-Athir's Usd al-Ghaba (entry 5065) gives him as al-Mughira ibn Nawfal ibn al-Harith ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib al-Qurashi al-Hashimi, born in Mecca before the Hijra in the Prophet's lifetime; one report says he knew only six years of the Prophet's life. His kunya was Abu Yahya (also reported as Abu Halima). When Ibn Muljam struck 'Ali, al-Mughira, described as very strong, threw a cloak over him and wrestled him to the ground; he later married Umama bint Abi al-'As per 'Ali's instruction. No death year is given.

bio: Ibn 'Abd al-Barr's al-Isti'ab (entry 1568) gives his kunya as Abu Suhayl and says he made the second emigration to Abyssinia, then returned to Mecca, where his father Suhayl detained him and tried to turn him from Islam. He went out to Badr with his father, then left the polytheists for the Prophet and witnessed Badr and later battles; he was a witness to the Treaty of Hudaybiya and secured safe conduct for his father at the conquest of Mecca. It states he was martyred at al-Yamama in the year 12, aged 38.

No death year is given.

bio: Arabic Wikipedia describes Ashama ibn Abjar as the Negus (king) of Aksum (Abyssinia), who gave sanctuary to the Muslim emigrants and refused Quraysh's envoys after hearing Ja'far ibn Abi Talib recite from the Qur'an. It gives his death as Rajab 9 AH / October 630 CE, and says the Prophet told his Companions to pray for their brother who had died in a foreign land, performing the funeral prayer in absentia. It cites Ibn Kathir's al-Bidaya wa al-Nihaya among its sources.

bio: Ibn Sa'd's al-Tabaqat al-Kubra (entry 4528, women of Banu Salima) names her mother as Hind bint Malik ibn 'Amir of Banu Bayada and her husband as 'Abdullah ibn al-Humayr of Ashja', an ally of Banu 'Ubaid of Banu Salima. It states she accepted Islam and gave the pledge to the Prophet.
research_evidence: أم ثابت بنت حارثة بن زيد بن ثعلبة بن عبيد بن عدي بن غنم بن كعب بن سلمة
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)
